steps.where: js/deals.js (new, IIFE `Deals`, modelled on js/pacts.js:41-204); script tag after js/pacts.js in index.html:101, dev.html:116, tests/run.html:106
steps.detail: State: `deals` Map id->record, `offers` Map id->record, `seq`, `offerSeq`. Deal record: { id:'d'+seq, a, b (a<b, pacts.js:46 convention), since (World.getTurn() at signing), duration (one of deal.durations), autoRenew, priceMult, flows:[{i, dir:'ab'|'ba', vol, price}], paid:0, status:'live'|'renewed'|'expired'|'void', endedTurn:null, reason:null|'expired'|'lapsed'|'renewed'|'died', renewedFrom:null }. Units: vol = $M per turn at index 100 (tradeFlows' vol, clipped); price = Market.getPrices()[i] at signing; value per turn = vol*price/100 in $M (same expression as moves.js:343); money = value*1e6 dollars. Derived, never stored: until = since+duration; left(t) = until-(t+1) after the tick closing turn t. API: live(a,b), forNation(nid), get(id), committed(nid) -> {bySector[6] net vol (sells +, buys -), value}, income(nid,tune) -> per-turn $M, sign(plan) , propose/accept/decline/counter/offersFor/waiting(nid), tick(tune, turn, {player}), reset, serialize, loadState, count.

steps.step: Add the term tunables, placeholders only
steps.where: js/tunables.js, new group 'Deals' next to the trade group at 588-658; each with label/doc/min/max/step or kind so tests/tunables.test.js:10-22 passes
steps.detail: deal.durations kind 'array' [2,4,8,20] (D163, DECISIONS.md:2343); deal.defaultDuration 4 (what the Move signs when the intent carries no terms — the AI in A1 and the UI's opening value); deal.defaultAutoRenew kind 'bool' false; deal.countdownAt kind 'array' [4,2,1]; deal.offerTurns 2 (an open offer's own expiry); deal.maxOpenOffers 3 (A4's incoming cap, enforced in propose from day one); deal.priceMultMin 0.5 and deal.priceMultMax 1.5 (range of the negotiable split). No literal anywhere in deals.js or moves.js.

steps.step: planTrade grows terms and reads commitments; resolveTrade signs instead of paying
steps.detail: Intent: {type:'trade', nid, target, terms?:{duration, autoRenew, priceMult, volumes?:{[i]:vol}}}; missing terms fall back to deal.defaultDuration / deal.defaultAutoRenew / 1.0 / full match. Checks in order: both alive; not self; adjacent (395); Deals.live(nid,target) -> refuse 'You already have a deal with X — it runs N more turns; renegotiate when it expires' (replaces 398-401); Recognition.canTrade (407-412 unchanged); duration must be in deal.durations; priceMult inside [priceMultMin, priceMultMax]. Availability: flows = tradeFlows(nid,target) with each side's surplus reduced by Deals.committed(side).bySector (sells already promised reduce the surplus, buys already promised reduce the deficit) — a read-side subtraction, Market untouched; capacity = min(tradeCapacity(nid).total - committed(nid).value, same for target); applyCapacity as today (413-414); then clip each vol to terms.volumes if given. Preview: flows (with price snapshot), duration, until, autoRenew, priceMult, incomeA/incomeB per turn ($M, from the split rule in step 4), gain = incomeA (so js/ai.js:319 scores the proposer's per-turn take as before), termTotal = gain*duration, effects [{'Per turn, each side'...},{'Turns',duration},{'Sectors traded',n}]. resolveTrade: Game.batch(() => { Deals.sign(plan) ; markTraded both ways (377-380); Relations.record('traded') both ways (452-453) }); keep Market.update (455); log kind 'trade', event 'signed', dealId, partner, terms [{name:'Duration',value,key:'deal.durations'},{name:'Per turn, each side',value:gain,key:'trade.gain'}], text 'A and B signed a N-turn deal worth Xm a turn to each'. legal: `if (!Deals.live(nid, other))` at 1299. No payment at signing: the first settlement is the tick that closes the signing turn, so the player sees income the same End turn the click used to pay on.

steps.step: Define what 'price' means on a money-only economy: index snapshot, plus a negotiable split of the joint gain
steps.where: js/deals.js settlement arithmetic; js/moves.js planTrade preview
steps.detail: For each flow f with seller S and buyer B: value = vol*price/100; S earns value*priceMult*trade.gain, B earns value*(2-priceMult)*trade.gain. At priceMult=1 this is byte-for-byte today's rule (moves.js:418, 443-444: each side earns total*trade.gain), and the sum of the two incomes never changes with the multiplier — it moves the existing joint gain between the parties, exactly as the transit toll slider moves a benefit (actions.js:585-586, 609-610). This is the only meaning a counter-offer on 'price' can have while nothing moves: a true buyer-pays-seller price would leave every buyer worse off on an economy where buying has no modelled benefit (the hollow spot, addendum §3), so it waits for 'goods move' (addendum §4 row 1) and the §4.1 multiplier stack (row 5). The market index is untouched and stays the base price (spec §1.5).

steps.step: Settle live deals once per world turn, inside the batch
steps.where: js/world.js:1214 — new line `Deals.tick(tn, turn, { player: Game.getPlayer() });` immediately before Game.tickTreasuries() (1215), after phaseSecession (1162), Relations.forget (1170) and Pacts.tick (1173); unconditional (no Complexity gate, complexity.js:20-21)
steps.detail: tick(tune, t, {player}) walks deals in ascending id order. (1) Void: if !Game.getNation(a) or !Game.getNation(b) -> status 'void', reason 'died', endedTurn t, no payment this tick, ledger kind 'trade' event 'void' (subject = survivor, partner = the dead id, text 'X's deal with Y died with Y'). (2) Pay: for every status 'live' deal with since <= t < since+duration, compute incA/incB by the step-4 rule in flow order, Game.earn(a, incA*1e6), Game.earn(b, incB*1e6), paid++. Per turn, not lump sum: 'volume per turn' is what tradeCapacity is documented in (game.js:1321), a lump sum would make a 20-turn deal a 20x click, and only per-turn payment makes a mid-term death cost anything. Deal income is NOT folded into Game.treasuryFlow (game.js:1535-1604) — that query is read by Power solvency, QoL strain, aid and the AI's income normalisation, and changing it is a behaviour change across the full game; Deals.income(nid) is the query for panels. (3) Countdown: left = since+duration-(t+1); if left is in deal.countdownAt AND a party is `player`, ledger kind 'trade' event 'countdown', left, dealId, subject = the player party, partner = the other (the journal's 'Yours' filter at journal.js:75-77 matches on subject). AI-AI deals get no countdown entries (50 nations x 3 lines per term is a newspaper nobody reads; the deal ledger derives everyone's countdown from left()). (4) Expiry when left === 0 — step 6. (5) Offers whose expires <= t are dropped; ledger event 'offer-lapsed' only when `to` is the player. Relations are NOT recorded per settlement (0.12/turn against rel.decay 0.94 clamps standing at +1 inside ~15 turns), and tradeCooldown is NOT re-stamped per settlement (a stamp at signing/renewal keeps the partner inside nation.historyWindow=20 for the whole of any term, so power.js:912 counts it, and Actions' transit button at actions.js:489 is not disabled by a live deal).

steps.step: Expiry, auto-renew and the renegotiation prompt
steps.where: js/deals.js tick step (4); js/moves.js planTrade is the re-plan
steps.detail: At left === 0, after the final payment: rePlan = Moves.plan({type:'trade', nid:a, target:b, terms:{duration, autoRenew, priceMult, volumes: old vols}}, tune) — this re-fixes price at today's index, re-clips volume to today's availability and capacity, and re-checks alive/adjacent/canTrade through the one rulebook. (a) autoRenew && rePlan.ok: sign a NEW record (new id, since = t+1 so there is no double payment this tick, renewedFrom = old id); old -> status 'renewed'; markTraded + Relations 'traded' both ways; ledger event 'renewed' with terms showing old vs new per-turn income so the re-price is visible. (b) autoRenew && !rePlan.ok: old -> 'expired', reason 'lapsed'; ledger event 'lapsed' carrying rePlan.reason (nothing to trade / no recognition / no longer adjacent / partner gone). (c) !autoRenew: old -> 'expired', reason 'expired'; ledger event 'expired'; if a party is `player` and rePlan.ok, Deals.propose({kind:'renew', from: counterparty, to: player, dealId, terms: rePlan's terms, prices: rePlan's snapshot, expires: t+deal.offerTurns}) — this is the RENEGOTIATION PROMPT: js/shell.js completeTurn adds `if (Deals.waiting(you()) && showDealOffer()) return true;` beside the crisis halt at shell.js:250 (the card itself is the UI area's), so fastForward (266-275) stops on it like any other halt. If neither party is the player, nothing further happens: AI re-initiation is A4. 'Lost surplus mid-term' is therefore answered here and only here: volume and price are both held for the term (money-only, nothing fails to arrive), and the loss bites at renewal, where the re-plan is smaller or refused. Lost adjacency mid-term is likewise checked at renewal only; the mid-term route break with a reason belongs to A2/A3.

steps.step: Offers as model state, shaped for A4
steps.detail: Offer: { id:'o'+offerSeq, from, to, kind:'new'|'counter'|'renew', dealId|null, replyTo|null, made:t, expires: made+deal.offerTurns, terms:{duration, autoRenew, priceMult, flows:[{i,dir,vol,price}]} } — prices are snapshotted at offer time because an offer is a price you were quoted. propose refuses when Deals.live(from,to) or when `to` already holds deal.maxOpenOffers unexpired incoming offers. accept(id, tune): Moves.plan on the offer's terms (alive/adjacent/canTrade/availability re-checked, volumes clipped to today's), then sign at the OFFER's prices; refuses with plan.reason otherwise. counter(id, terms): drops the original, proposes kind 'counter' the other way with replyTo — counters may change duration, priceMult and volumes (addendum A1 bullet 3). decline(id) drops it. waiting(nid) = any unexpired offer addressed to nid. In A1 offers are created by the player's negotiation flow (UI area, calling propose/counter/accept) and by the tick's renewal prompt; AI-AI deals in A1 sign directly through the Move with default terms, both sides agreeing by construction exactly as the click did. The acceptance policy for a player's proposal is the negotiation area's; the model gives it everything it needs because Moves.plan with terms yields both parties' per-turn income.

steps.where: js/statedoc.js:94 (assemble: `deals: Deals.serialize()` after pacts), :183 (applyModel: `Deals.loadState(doc.deals)` after Pacts, before Events — Game.loadState at 178 has already run), :197 (STATEFUL_MODULES += 'Deals'); tests/saves.test.js:277 mods list += Deals; resets at js/app.js:186, js/sim.js:147, tests/world-fixture.js:77 (`Deals.reset()` beside Pacts.reset())
steps.detail: serialize -> { seq, offerSeq, deals:[plain copies, flows copied], offers:[plain copies] }: only finite numbers, strings, booleans and null (no Infinity, Sets or typed arrays) so tests/saves.test.js:255-271's byte-identical JSON round trip holds. loadState(null|undefined) -> empty, so a version-3 document written before A1 loads with no deals; no VERSION bump (js/statedoc.js:52), the same way Pacts arrived without one. loadState rebuilds the Maps in array order, so iteration order after a load equals before.

All deal entries use kind 'trade' with an `event` field: signed | renewed | countdown | expired | lapsed | void | offer | offer-lapsed, plus dealId, partner, left. Signing entries come from moves.js:70 log() (phase 'action'); tick entries use phase 'deal'. This keeps tests/ai.test.js:253 (every kind is in Ledger.KINDS), journal.js:68 and ledger.js:122-128 untouched. DESIGN.md's Trade section replaces 'Each partner is on a cooldown' with the standing-deal rules (terms, per-turn settlement, price held, one live deal per pair, expiry/renewal/prompt, death voids), §12 drops the 'what trade lacks is TERMS' gap, and the nation-record line notes deals live in js/deals.js.

newTunables: deal.durations — kind 'array', [2, 4, 8, 20] turns (six months, one year, two years, five years; D163)
deal.defaultDuration — 4, range 1..40 step 1: the term the trade Move signs when the intent carries none (the AI in A1; the UI's opening value)
deal.countdownAt — kind 'array', [4, 2, 1]: turns-left values at which a player's deal writes a countdown entry
deal.offerTurns — 2, range 1..20 step 1: how many turns an open offer (new, counter or renewal) stays on the table
deal.maxOpenOffers — 3, range 1..20 step 1: incoming offers a nation may hold at once (A4's cap, placed now so the object is ready)
deal.priceMultMin — 0.5 and deal.priceMultMax — 1.5, range 0.1..1 / 1..3 step 0.05: bounds of the negotiable split of the joint gain; 1.0 reproduces today's symmetric deal exactly
(none for the per-turn rate: trade.gain is reused; trade.cooldownTurns keeps its value and gets a doc line saying it now governs external sales and transit only)
scopeCheck: No step touches demand, supply or the price index. Demand: market.demandShare and Market.nationSurplus (market.js:103-117) are read at signing/renewal and never written; the 'available surplus' used by planTrade is nationSurplus minus what live deals already commit, computed in Moves/Deals as a read-side subtraction. Supply: Market.areaProduction / Market.update (market.js:42-75) are untouched and settlement never calls update. Price index: Market.getPrices() is snapshotted into the deal at signing and never modified; the negotiated priceMult moves the existing joint gain between the two parties and changes no published price. The one genuine tension, raised rather than planned around: on this economy a negotiated PRICE can only be a split of the symmetric gain, because buying has no modelled benefit until goods move (addendum §4 row 1) — a real buyer-pays-seller price would make every buyer refuse. Not a blocker for A1 (the default split is today's rule byte for byte), but it is Aaron's to confirm that 'counter-offers may modify price' means this in A1.
determinism: Deal and offer ids are 'd'+seq / 'o'+offerSeq from counters that live in the module and in the save (the Ledger.seq pattern, ledger.js:34,82,200; Game.seq, game.js:1034), never from turn or time. Settlement iterates deals in ascending id order (Map insertion order, re-established by loadState from the serialized array), and sums each party's income in flow index order, so a save/load mid-term reproduces the same treasuries to the bit. No randomness in A1: the tick takes `rng` in its signature for A4 but draws nothing; any future draw uses rng.stream('deals') (rng.js:93-100) so the 'ai', 'unite', 'turnorder' and 'drift' streams are unchanged. The AI signs default terms deterministically through the existing Moves.plan/legal path; the only AI randomness is the existing softmax draw on rng.stream('ai') (ai.js:619). Player-dependent behaviour (offers, countdown entries, the halt) keys off Game.getPlayer(), which is part of the saved state (game.js:1745). Same seed, same sequence of player actions, same run: fingerprint() already includes treasuries (world-fixture.js:211), so the existing determinism tests (ai.test.js:188-195, player.test.js:141-147, invariants.test.js:167-178) guard settlement, and a new test compares JSON.stringify(Deals.serialize()) across two runs.
risks: Income scale: a standing deal pays every turn what the click paid once per trade.cooldownTurns+1 = 4 turns, so trade income per partner rises ~4x (more with 20-turn auto-renew). Treasuries swell; Power's solvency term, aid amounts (aid.shareOfTreasury) and annex affordability shift in the full game whenever the AI signs. The rule is not to tune; the knob is trade.gain and the alpha is the place to watch it. Any test pinned on absolute treasury magnitudes after AI rounds would move — none found (unverified).
The meaning of 'price' (step 4) is a design ruling, not a code fact: if Aaron rules price non-negotiable in A1, drop priceMult; the default path is identical either way.

'Lost surplus mid-term holds the term' is the deliberate choice; the alternative (short delivery: pay on min(vol, current surplus)) is the stakes mechanic that belongs to 'goods move' and would make every war-damaged nation's deals shrink silently. If Aaron wants that bite before alpha it is a five-line change in the tick, but it is the post-alpha item by the addendum's own table.

AI cadence changes shape: legal() now excludes partners with a live deal rather than cooled-down ones, and the AI is indifferent to duration (always deal.defaultDuration) until A4. Over 20 AI rounds the kinds present (ai.test.js:248-250) should still include annex/war; if trade income makes annexation affordable more often the mix moves but the test holds.
Committed capacity is a per-nation total; A2's per-mode caps (Highway/Rail/Port) will have to split it. Flag for the A2 plan so it does not double-count.
Ledger volume: countdown entries are player-only, so ledger.cap (4000) is not at risk; if the UI area decides all deals should announce, revisit.
A save from before A1 loads with no deals but its nations may hold tradeCooldown stamps from clicks — harmless (the field means the same thing).
No treaty succession: a nation absorbed by unite loses every deal at the next tick with reason 'died'. Spec §5.8's limbo is Phase 7; the ledger says plainly what happened so a tester can report it.
Adjacency and recognition are checked at signing and renewal only; a deal between two nations that stop touching mid-term keeps paying until expiry. A2/A3 own the mid-term route break and its reason.
tests: A signed 4-turn deal pays each party its per-turn value x trade.gain x 1e6 at each of the next four World.advanceTurn calls (measured net of Game.treasuryFlow(nid).delta) and nothing at the fifth.
The price is held: advance until Market.getPrices() differs from the signing snapshot, and the settlement amount still equals the recorded flows' vol x recorded price / 100, not the current index.
Volume is per turn: deals of duration 2 and 8 on identical flows pay the same amount per tick and their term totals differ by exactly 4x.
planTrade refuses a second deal with a partner while one is live, names the turns remaining in its reason, and allows one on the tick after expiry.

Committed surplus: after A signs away all of its Agriculture surplus to B, planTrade(A, C) shows no Agriculture flow and A's remaining capacity for a deal with C is tradeCapacity.total minus the live deal's value.
A party dying mid-term (Game.mergeInto) voids the deal at the next tick with reason 'died', pays nothing that tick, and writes a kind 'trade' event 'void' entry naming the survivor as subject.

With autoRenew on, expiry signs a new record with a fresh id, since = t+1, renewedFrom set, prices re-fixed at the then-current index and volume re-clipped to the then-current surplus; the old record reads status 'renewed'.

With autoRenew off and the player a party, expiry leaves a kind 'renew' offer in Deals.waiting(player) whose expires equals t + deal.offerTurns and whose terms equal the re-plan; with no player party nothing is offered.
Countdown entries appear exactly at left values in deal.countdownAt for a player's 8-turn deal (4, 2, 1) and never for an AI-AI deal.
Offers lapse on the tick where expires <= t; propose refuses a fourth incoming offer under deal.maxOpenOffers and refuses while Deals.live(from, to).

priceMult = 1 pays both sides exactly what the pre-A1 resolveTrade formula would have (total x trade.gain); priceMult = 1.5 leaves the sum of the two incomes unchanged and moves it toward the net seller.
Determinism: two runs of bootWorld(seed) + 12 x AI.round give equal fingerprint() and equal JSON.stringify(Deals.serialize()).
Save round trip: Deals.serialize -> JSON -> loadState -> serialize is deepEqual, and a tick after the reload pays the same treasuries as a tick without it.
StateDoc.assemble carries a 'deals' section, STATEFUL_MODULES names Deals, and tests/saves.test.js:277's mods list includes it; bootWorld leaves Deals.count() at 0 across suites.

After 20 AI rounds with deals, every ledger entry still has a kind in Ledger.KINDS and readable text (the existing invariant at tests/ai.test.js:253), and deal entries carry event, dealId and partner.
Every deal.* schema key passes tests/tunables.test.js's label/doc/range check; deal.durations contains exactly 2, 4, 8 and 20.
Economy mode (Complexity.applyPreset('economy')): a deal signs and settles with recognition switched off.
The trade Move with no terms signs at deal.defaultDuration and deal.defaultAutoRenew, and Moves.legal still lists 'trade' for neighbours without a live deal (tests/moves.test.js:389 keeps passing).
unverified: Recognition is grant-only (no revoke path), so 'lost recognition mid-term' cannot happen — js/recognition.js shows grant/founded/tick; a revoke was not found but the file was not read end to end.
No existing test pins absolute treasury levels after AI rounds; searched tests for treasury assertions only by grep.
Pacts (M11.2) was added after save VERSION 3 (M9.6) without a bump — inferred from milestone numbering, not from git history; the no-bump precedent for adding a top-level document key rests on that.
Nothing switches on ledger `phase` (journal.js and ledger.js filter on kind; panels.js not read in full), so phase 'deal' is safe.
The economy's sector order [Ag, Extraction, Manufacturing, Trade, Finance, IT] is taken from the tunables docs (tunables.js:91, 585), not from opening data/economy.json.
